title: AI is shaking software. There's a new way to spot which companies are built to survive.
excerpt: Which software companies can survive the AI era? Barclays highlights the firms best positioned to weather the disruption.
content_html:
By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

If AI really is coming for the software industry, which companies have the best chance of making it through?

This has been on my mind again this week after the gruesome acquisition of Airtable. This former SaaS startup darling was valued at more than $11 billion during the pandemic tech boom in 2021. It sells a tool for organizing work and related information. On Tuesday, it was acquired for $1.3 billion.

Later in the week, HubSpot, a major SaaS vendor, plunged after disappointing guidance. But Atlassian surged after much better results.

The SaaS sector has been pummeled this year by investors worrying whether some of these companies will even survive. So, how do you spot survivors in the wreckage?

Barclays strategists tried to answer that question by looking backward instead of forward. They studied five major technology shakeups from the past: the rise of digital advertising, streaming, smartphones, online shopping, and shale gas. They looked at what separated the companies that survived from the ones that didn't.

The answer wasn't what you might expect.

The winners weren't necessarily the fastest-growing companies or the ones that spent the most money. Instead, the survivors tended to share four traits: healthy profit margins, strong cash generation, low debt, and high employee productivity. Those qualities gave management more room to adapt when their industry suddenly changed.

It's a useful reminder as the SaaSpocalypse debate gathers pace. Much of the conversation around AI has focused on who has the smartest models or the flashiest product demos. Barclays argues those may not be the defining factors. When an entire industry is under pressure, financial strength and operational discipline may matter more than rapid growth. Companies with healthy profits can absorb shocks. Those carrying less debt have more flexibility to change direction. Efficient businesses simply have more options.

Using those characteristics, Barclays created a "Resilient Software" basket. AppLovin, Freshworks, and InterDigital ranked highest across the broader software universe. Looking only at software companies that Barclays already rates positively, Datadog, Veeva Systems, and Zscaler came out on top, followed by Microsoft, Intuit, PTC, Autodesk, Salesforce, Palo Alto Networks, and ServiceNow.

No screen can predict who will win the AI era. But this framework offers a refreshing way to think about the software industry. The companies most likely to survive may not be the ones racing fastest. They may simply be the ones with the strongest balance sheets and the most room to maneuver as AI rewrites the rules.

如果人工智能真的进入软件行业，哪些公司最有机会渡过难关？

本周，在可怕地收购了 Airtable 之后，这个问题再次出现在我的脑海中。 这家前 SaaS 初创公司宠儿在 2021 年科技大流行期间估值超过 110 亿美元。 它销售一种用于组织工作和相关信息的工具。 周二，它被以 13 亿美元收购。

本周晚些时候，主要 SaaS 供应商 HubSpot 在业绩指引令人失望后股价暴跌。 但 Atlassian 在取得更好的业绩后股价飙升。

SaaS 行业今年遭受了投资者的重创，他们担心其中一些公司是否能生存下来。 那么，如何在废墟中找到幸存者呢？

巴克莱策略师试图通过向后看而不是向前看来回答这个问题。 他们研究了过去的五次重大技术变革：数字广告、流媒体、智能手机、在线购物和页岩气的兴起。 他们研究了存活下来的公司与失败的公司之间的区别。

答案并不是你所期望的。

赢家不一定是增长最快的公司或花费最多资金的公司。 相反，幸存者往往具有四个共同特征：健康的利润率、强劲的现金生成能力、低债务和高员工生产力。 当行业突然发生变化时，这些品质为管理层提供了更多的适应空间。

随着 SaaS 末日辩论的步伐加快，这是一个有用的提醒。 关于人工智能的大部分讨论都集中在谁拥有最智能的模型或最华丽的产品演示。 巴克莱认为这些可能不是决定性因素。 当整个行业面临压力时，财务实力和运营纪律可能比快速增长更重要。 利润稳健的公司可以吸收冲击。 那些负债较少的人可以更灵活地改变方向。 高效的企业只是有更多的选择。

利用这些特征，巴克莱创建了一个“弹性软件”篮子。 AppLovin、Freshworks 和 InterDigital 在更广泛的软件领域排名最高。 仅考虑巴克莱已经给予积极评价的软件公司，Datadog、Veeva Systems 和 Zscaler 名列前茅，其次是 Microsoft、Intuit、PTC、Autodesk、Salesforce、Palo Alto Networks 和 ServiceNow。

没有屏幕可以预测谁将赢得人工智能时代。 但这个框架提供了一种令人耳目一新的方式来思考软件行业。 最有可能生存下来的公司可能并不是跑得最快的公司。 当人工智能重写规则时，它们可能只是拥有最强大的资产负债表和最大的回旋余地的人。
